verdict.rationale: PagerDuty's own docs show it ships on-call schedules that map coverage needs and decide who gets notified, and escalation policies route incidents to those schedules. The pack does not show the depth the story asks for: rotations, layers, time zones and round-robin coverage are never described. Missing for 10: documented rotation configuration, schedule layers, time-zone handling, round-robin coverage, and independent or hands-on corroboration of schedule building.

support.subject: As an SRE, I can build on-call schedules with rotations, layers, time zones, and round-robin coverage that match how my teams actually work

citations.quote: Use legacy schedules to map your coverage needs and determine who receives a notification when an incident triggers.
Escalation policies automate incident assignment and connect services to individual users and/or schedules.
monitors calendars, detects potential conflicts, identifies qualified replacements, and coordinates schedule changes without manual intervention
